catalog_quote: [Hertsens 1940: 271, Northern Lendu; scanned text layer, diacritics stripped] Dans cette etude nous ne parlerons que du groupe nord, nos etudes ayant eu trait principalement a ce groupe. Que le mot ‘ lendu ’ dans cette etude soit done toujours pris dans le sens ‘ lendu-nord ’. Le lendu est une langue isolante a caracteristiques soudanaises-est; mots strictement monosyllabiques, absence d’inflexions (incluant absence de genre grammatical et de systeme de classes); le genitif est place avant le mot qui le gouverne; langue a tonemes (les tons ont une valeur semantique et grammaticale). new_statements.quote: Larochette reports a tendency towards stress on the penultimate syllable of a word or phrase in MANGBETU, accompanied sometimes by extra high tone as in neka-'kidri, headache. No such uniformity of stress pattern, however, has been found in the other Language Groups. Even such intimately closely allied languages as MORU and MA'DI have quite different stress behaviour.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lendu is described as a tone language with three established tone levels; on stress the source says only that no uniform (predictable) stress pattern was found for the LENDU group (or for MORU-MA'DI and MANGBUTU-EFE), in contrast to the penultimate tendency reported for Mangbetu. No Lendu word is cited and no placement rule is given; this cannot be read as fixed, weight-sensitive or lexical stress -- only as 'no uniform pattern found'.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Lendu; the same section gives Moru initial stress ('iza) versus Ma'di final stress (i'za) as the contrasting cases, and notes that in both 'words within a phrase retain their original stress'.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement covering the whole LENDU group (chapter examples are from Northern Lendu = Bbadha, lend1245); word-level ('stress pattern'); text reconstructed from Open Library full-text search snippets of an access-restricted scan (scanned as indexed), so wording is reliable but page number is inferred. The open, saved primary phonology sources (Trifkovic 1977a, 1977b) are silent on stress and describe 3-4 level tones plus a rising contour.
new_statements.identity_note: All material concerns Lendu proper / Northern Lendu (Bbadha, Kilendu; lend1245). Tucker & Bryan 1966 state their LENDU examples are 'from N. LENDU unless otherwise indicated'. Hertsens 1940 splits 'le lendu ou ba dha' into a northern group (dialects north of 1°35'N) and a southern group 'parlés au pays de Géty' -- the latter is Ngiti (ngit1239, Glottolog's separate language), so any statement in Hertsens must be checked for which group it covers. Dhejju 1977 describes the Tadha dialect; Trifkovic 1977 does not name a dialect (informants M. Njabu, husband and wife; 'North Eastern Zaire').
